LoloBuy tracking number not showing: a buyer checklist

Separate the package record from the carrier waybill, then collect the right evidence before asking for support.

⌕

Tracking and support · 10 minute read

LoloBuy tracking number not showing: identify the missing record first

If your LoloBuy tracking number is not showing, the first question is not “Where is my shipment?” It is “Which number and which stage am I looking at?” LoloBuy’s current parcel interface separates a package number from a waybill number. The package number identifies the parcel inside the account. The waybill number identifies the shipment record used for logistics tracking.

A submitted package can therefore exist before a carrier-facing waybill appears. The package may still be waiting for payment, processing, a risk check or dispatch. A missing waybill in those stages is different from a waybill that appears but returns no tracking events.

This guide helps you diagnose the exact gap, preserve useful evidence and ask support one answerable question without guessing a delivery date or declaring the parcel lost.

1. Do not use the package number as the tracking number

Open the parcel record and locate the fields labelled Package number and Waybill number. Save both when they are present. The package number is the stable reference for finding the transaction in My Parcel and for discussing packing, payment or parcel status. The waybill number is the reference shown with the shipment’s logistics information.

Copy the waybill from its labelled field rather than from an email subject, payment record or warehouse item page. Remove accidental spaces before pasting it into any tracking field. Do not substitute the original product order number, warehouse item number, rehearsal number or payment bill number. Those records describe different stages.

If the account shows a package number but the waybill field is blank or marked unavailable, record that exact condition. It is clearer than saying “tracking does not work,” which can mean several different problems.

2. Check the package status before expecting a waybill

LoloBuy currently distinguishes parcel states including Pending payment, Processing, Risk control, Shipped, Canceled and Completed. Read the status on the same parcel record as the missing waybill. A payment confirmation, warehouse item or rehearsal result is not proof that the international package has reached the Shipped stage.

Pending payment means the parcel payment step is not complete in the platform record. Processing means the parcel is still being handled. Risk control is a separate platform state, so it should not be interpreted as carrier movement. Shipped is the state that most directly supports expecting shipment information. Canceled is not a trackable shipment, and Completed represents a later parcel state.

Do not infer a fixed handoff time from the status name. Route, packaging and operational conditions can differ. Use the live status, submission time, shipping method and account messages as the evidence available for your parcel.

3. Separate “no waybill” from “no tracking events”

These problems require different checks. No waybill means the parcel detail does not yet show a carrier shipment reference. No tracking events means a waybill exists, but the Shipment tracking area is empty or has no new scan. The current interface can display “No tracking events yet,” which describes the record but does not identify the cause.

For no waybill, focus on parcel status, payment, final shipping adjustments, risk messages and dispatch. For no events, focus on the exact waybill, shipping method, the last visible event and whether the account has received a logistics update. Do not mix the two in one support message.

A parcel can also move through more than one logistics system. The number shown in LoloBuy is the starting point; a later local-delivery reference may appear only if the route or carrier supplies it. Never invent a local number by changing characters in the original waybill.

4. Confirm that you opened the correct parcel

Buyers who submit several packages close together can easily inspect the wrong record. Compare the parcel’s item list, submission time, destination country, shipping method and recipient information with your own records. Confirm that the parcel contains the products you expected and that the address belongs to the intended shipment.

Check for similarly named products split across different packages. A rehearsal can also have its own record before an actual package is submitted, so a rehearsal number should not be treated as a shipment reference. If the item list does not match, return to the parcel list and find the correct package number before escalating.

Keep screenshots wide enough to show the page label and number together. A cropped number without its field name makes it harder to tell whether it is an order, parcel, waybill or bill reference.

5. Review payment and site messages

The current parcel-payment guidance says a paid parcel enters sorting and shipping and can be tracked on the parcel page. It also says that a difference between estimated and actual shipping cost may lead to an additional-payment or refund notice through an in-site message. That makes the message center relevant when dispatch information has not appeared.

Check whether the account shows an unpaid balance, a refund notice, a risk-related message, an address question or another parcel-specific request. Read the message number and timestamp, then match it to the package number. Do not pay a second time merely because the carrier field is empty; first establish what the parcel record says is outstanding.

Also check the Notice Center for logistics updates that may apply broadly. A general announcement is context, not proof of what happened to one parcel. The package detail remains the primary transaction record.

6. Verify the shipping method and logistics panel

The Package Details page can show the destination country, shipping method, parcel status, waybill number and Tracking & logistics information. Capture all of these together. The shipping method helps support identify the relevant operational path, while the recipient and destination help detect an address mismatch.

If the waybill appears, use the View details or shipment-tracking area provided in the account. Record the full event text and timestamp rather than paraphrasing it. “No tracking events yet” is more precise than “carrier lost it.” Likewise, an export, customs or delivery event should be reported exactly as shown rather than translated into a conclusion.

Do not confirm receipt simply to see whether tracking changes. LoloBuy provides a Confirm receipt action for acknowledging that the package has been received. Use it only after you have the parcel, not as a troubleshooting button.

7. Build a support packet that answers the first questions

Before contacting support, collect the package number, parcel status, waybill field, shipping method, destination, submission time and last visible logistics event. Add screenshots of the parcel list and Package Details page. If an in-site message refers to the parcel, include that message without exposing passwords, verification codes or full payment-card data.

Write one chronological summary: “Package [number] shows Shipped. The Waybill number field is blank. Shipping method is [shown method]. I checked Package Details and in-site messages on [date and time]. Please confirm whether a waybill has been assigned to this package.” If a waybill exists but events are empty, replace the question with: “Please confirm whether this is the current tracking number and whether shipment data has been handed to the tracking system.”

This format names the account fact, the missing field and the requested clarification. Avoid sending repeated messages with different numbers. A single complete record is easier to investigate.

8. Escalate an abnormal trace without assuming the outcome

Once a waybill and events appear, monitor the latest scan and any account message. LoloBuy’s current shipping notice tells buyers to track the parcel, receive it promptly and contact the platform when tracking updates look abnormal. “Abnormal” should be tied to a visible event, contradiction or missing handoff—not an invented universal deadline.

If the account displays a parcel-protection or claim option for that shipment, read its rules, claim period and evidence requirements before filing. The current claim interface can ask for a loss type, affected goods, description and supporting evidence. The existence of that interface does not guarantee that every parcel, delay or missing scan is eligible.

Preserve the waybill, tracking screenshots, package photos, item list, outer-packaging photos and unboxing evidence when relevant. Do not manufacture a loss date or upload unrelated files. Describe only what the record proves and let the applicable process determine the result.

Final LoloBuy tracking-number checklist

First, locate the correct package and distinguish its package number from the waybill number. Check the parcel status, payment record, shipping method, destination, item list and in-site messages. Then decide whether the problem is a missing waybill or an existing waybill with no events.

Copy the labelled fields exactly, capture the page context and send one narrow support question. Do not promise yourself a scan time, guess a local carrier number, pay twice or confirm receipt early. A clean record cannot control the carrier, but it gives LoloBuy support the identifiers needed to investigate the right parcel.
